newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia-Cuba oil-sugar barter may change -Tass.
newsitem.headline: Russia-Cuba oil-sugar barter may change -Tass.

text.p: Russia and Cuba may seek new ways to cooperate economically given the problems behind recent oil-for-sugar barter deals, the main form of trade between the two, Prime-Tass news agency said on Wednesday.

It said Cuban Foreign Trade Minister Ricardo Cabrisas met Russian officials in Moscow on Wednesday to discuss foreign trade between the two allies, which mostly takes the form of Moscow selling oil to Havana in exchange for Cuban raws.

It said 85 percent of the $1.1 billion trade between the two countries last year was via oil-for-sugar barter deals. Russian imports of Cuban products totalled $521.5 million and Cuban imports of Russian products were valued at $625 million, according to Russian Foreign Trade Ministry figures.
Under an intergovernmental protocol covering 1996-1998, Russia supplied 1.8 million tonnes of crude oil to Cuba last year in exchange for over 850,000 tonnes of Cuban raws.

Supplies in 1997 are supposed to total six million tonnes of Russian oil in exchange for two million tonnes of raws. Delays in some of the deals have meant some of the deliveries cover the previous year's agreements, Tass said.

It said total Russian imports of Cuban raws last year were 1.8 million tonnes, including 0.9 million tonnes supplied by third-country suppliers, meaning commodities traders. Traders sold Russia 0.8 million tonnes of Cuban raws in the first five months of this year, Tass said.
